subject: EN
prompt: Which tense? 'I usually watch TV in the evening.'
explanation:
🎯 SIMPLE PRESENT

📖 USE:
For habits and regular actions.

✏️ SIGNAL WORDS:
• usually, always, often
• every day, sometimes
• never

💡 EXAMPLE:
'I USUALLY watch TV'
→ 'usually' = habit/regular action
→ Simple Present!

📐 FORMATION:
Infinitive (+ -s/-es for he/she/it)

✅ Answer: Simple Present

subject: EN
prompt: Which tense? 'They are calling their grandma right now.'
explanation:
🎯 PRESENT PROGRESSIVE

📖 USE:
For actions happening RIGHT NOW.

✏️ SIGNAL WORDS:
• right now, now
• at the moment
• Look! Listen!

💡 EXAMPLE:
'They ARE CALLING right now'
→ Action is happening NOW
→ Present Progressive!

📐 FORMATION:
am/is/are + verb + -ing

✅ Answer: Present Progressive

subject: EN
prompt: Which tense? 'He has lived here since 2003.'
explanation:
🎯 PRESENT PERFECT

📖 USE:
Action started in the past and continues to the present.

✏️ SIGNAL WORDS:
• since, for
• already, yet
• just, recently
• ever, never

💡 EXAMPLE:
'He HAS LIVED here SINCE 2003'
→ Started in 2003, still living there now
→ Present Perfect!

📐 FORMATION:
have/has + past participle

✅ Answer: Present Perfect

subject: EN
prompt: Fill in the correct form: 'I ___ just ___ at the airport.' (arrive - Present Perfect)
explanation:
🎯 PRESENT PERFECT FORMATION

📐 RULE:
have/has + past participle

✏️ HERE:
• Subject 'I' → use 'have' (not 'has')
• 'arrive' → past participle: 'arrived'

💡 'JUST' = very recently
→ Typical Present Perfect signal word!

✅ Answer: I HAVE just ARRIVED at the airport.

subject: EN
prompt: What is the Simple Past of 'go'?
explanation:
🎯 IRREGULAR VERB: GO

📐 FORMS:
• Simple Present: go
• Simple Past: WENT
• Past Participle: gone

⚠️ COMMON MISTAKE:
'goed' does NOT exist!
'go' is irregular!

💡 EXAMPLE:
• Yesterday I WENT to school.
• I have GONE to school. (Present Perfect)

✅ Answer: went

subject: EN
prompt: What is the Past Participle of 'write'?
explanation:
🎯 IRREGULAR VERB: WRITE

📐 FORMS:
• Simple Present: write
• Simple Past: wrote
• Past Participle: WRITTEN

💡 USE:
• Simple Past: She WROTE a letter yesterday.
• Present Perfect: She has WRITTEN a letter.

⚠️ REMEMBER:
write - wrote - written
(all different!)

✅ Answer: written

subject: EN
prompt: What is the Simple Past of 'see'?
explanation:
🎯 IRREGULAR VERB: SEE

📐 FORMS:
• Simple Present: see
• Simple Past: SAW
• Past Participle: seen

💡 EXAMPLES:
• I SAW him yesterday. (Simple Past)
• I have SEEN this movie before. (Present Perfect)

⚠️ CAREFUL:
'seed' is a noun (Samen)!
'sawed' is from 'saw' (sägen)!

✅ Answer: saw

subject: EN
prompt: What is the Past Participle of 'speak'?
explanation:
🎯 IRREGULAR VERB: SPEAK

📐 FORMS:
• Simple Present: speak
• Simple Past: spoke
• Past Participle: SPOKEN

💡 EXAMPLES:
• She SPOKE to him yesterday.
• She has SPOKEN to him already.

⚠️ PATTERN:
speak - spoke - spoken
(like break - broke - broken)

✅ Answer: spoken

subject: EN
prompt: What is the Simple Past AND Past Participle of 'put'?
explanation:
🎯 IRREGULAR VERB: PUT

📐 FORMS:
• Simple Present: put
• Simple Past: PUT
• Past Participle: PUT

💡 ALL FORMS ARE THE SAME!
put - put - put

📖 SIMILAR VERBS:
• cut - cut - cut
• shut - shut - shut
• hurt - hurt - hurt

✅ Answer: put - put

subject: EN
prompt: Choose the correct sentence:

choices: She has already finished her homework.
She have already finished her homework.
She has already finish her homework.
She already has finished her homework.

solution.correct_choice: She has already finished her homework.

explanation:
🎯 PRESENT PERFECT - WORD ORDER

📐 STRUCTURE:
Subject + have/has + (already/just/never) + past participle

✏️ ANALYSIS:
• 'She' (3rd person) → 'has' (not 'have')
• 'finish' → past participle: 'finished'
• 'already' comes AFTER have/has

⚠️ WRONG:
• 'She have...' (wrong auxiliary)
• 'She has finish...' (missing -ed)
• 'She already has...' (wrong word order)

✅ Answer: She has already finished her homework.

subject: EN
prompt: Which signal word indicates Present Perfect?
explanation:
🎯 SIGNAL WORDS

📖 PRESENT PERFECT:
• since, for
• already, yet
• just, recently
• ever, never
• so far, up to now

📖 SIMPLE PAST:
• yesterday
• last week/month/year
• ago

📖 SIMPLE PRESENT:
• every day, always
• usually, often

📖 PRESENT PROGRESSIVE:
• now, at the moment

✅ Answer: since (Present Perfect)

subject: EN
prompt: Which modal verb expresses OBLIGATION? 'You ___ wear a seatbelt.'
explanation:
🎯 MODAL VERBS: OBLIGATION

📖 MUST:
Expresses strong obligation/necessity.
'You MUST wear a seatbelt' = It's required!

📖 COMPARISON:
• must = strong obligation
• should = advice
• can = ability/permission
• might/could = possibility

💡 TIP:
'must' is often used for rules and laws.

✅ Answer: must

subject: EN
prompt: Which modal verb expresses ABILITY? 'She ___ speak three languages.'
explanation:
🎯 MODAL VERBS: ABILITY

📖 CAN:
Expresses ability (what someone is able to do).

'She CAN speak three languages'
= She is able to speak them.

📖 COMPARISON:
• can = ability NOW
• could = ability in the PAST
• will be able to = ability in FUTURE

✅ Answer: can

subject: EN
prompt: What is the comparative of 'good'?
explanation:
🎯 IRREGULAR COMPARISON

📐 FORMS OF 'GOOD':
• Positive: good
• Comparative: BETTER
• Superlative: best

⚠️ IRREGULAR!
'gooder' and 'more good' do NOT exist!

💡 SIMILAR:
• bad - worse - worst
• much/many - more - most
• little - less - least

✅ Answer: better

subject: EN
prompt: What is the superlative of 'beautiful'?
explanation:
🎯 COMPARISON: LONG ADJECTIVES

📐 RULE:
Adjectives with 3+ syllables:
• Comparative: more + adjective
• Superlative: most + adjective

✏️ 'BEAUTIFUL' (4 syllables):
• beautiful
• more beautiful
• THE MOST beautiful

⚠️ DON'T ADD -er/-est!
'beautifuler' is WRONG!

✅ Answer: the most beautiful

subject: EN
prompt: What does 'to spend money' mean in German?
explanation:
🎯 VOCABULARY: SPEND

📖 'to spend' has TWO meanings:
1. spend MONEY = Geld AUSGEBEN
2. spend TIME = Zeit VERBRINGEN

💡 EXAMPLES:
• I spent 50 euros on shoes. (ausgeben)
• I spent the weekend with friends. (verbringen)

📐 IRREGULAR:
spend - spent - spent

✅ Answer: Geld ausgeben

subject: EN
prompt: What does 'to lose' mean in German?
explanation:
🎯 VOCABULARY: LOSE

📖 'to lose' = verlieren

💡 EXAMPLES:
• I lost my keys. (Schlüssel verloren)
• We lost the game. (Spiel verloren)

📐 IRREGULAR:
lose - lost - lost

⚠️ DON'T CONFUSE:
• lose = verlieren
• leave = verlassen
• forget = vergessen

✅ Answer: verlieren

subject: EN
prompt: A sign says: 'Zeb throws objects. Please beware - his aim is accurate.' What does this mean?

choices: Be careful - this animal could hit you

solution.correct_choice: Be careful - this animal could hit you

explanation:
🎯 READING COMPREHENSION

📖 KEY WORDS:
• 'throws objects' = wirft Gegenstände
• 'beware' = Vorsicht
• 'aim is accurate' = Ziel ist genau

✏️ MEANING:
The animal throws things AND can aim well!
→ It could hit you!
→ This is a WARNING sign.

💡 TIP:
Look for KEY WORDS to understand the meaning!

✅ Answer: Be careful - this animal could hit you

subject: EN
prompt: Which question is correct?
explanation:
🎯 QUESTIONS IN SIMPLE PRESENT

📐 RULE:
Do/Does + subject + infinitive (WITHOUT -s)?

✏️ ANALYSIS:
• 'she' (3rd person) → use 'Does'
• After 'Does' → infinitive WITHOUT -s!
• 'like' (not 'likes'!)

⚠️ COMMON MISTAKE:
'Does she likes...' is WRONG!
The -s is already in 'Does'!

✅ Answer: Does she like pizza?

subject: EN
prompt: What is the Simple Past of 'think'?
explanation:
🎯 IRREGULAR VERB: THINK

📐 FORMS:
• Simple Present: think
• Simple Past: THOUGHT
• Past Participle: thought

⚠️ 'thinked' does NOT exist!

💡 SIMILAR PATTERN:
• think - thought - thought
• bring - brought - brought
• buy - bought - bought

✅ Answer: thought
